signals.text: We offer a broad, balanced, and ambitious curriculum that develops communication, independence, emotional regulation, and life skills — all underpinned by therapeutic support and EHCP outcomes.
Pupils have access to a broad and balanced curriculum, including regular outdoor learning through Forest School, to support confidence, teamwork and wellbeing.
A broad and balanced curriculum, focused on communication, independence, and preparation for adulthood.
Our curriculum is broad, balanced, and adapted to meet EHCP outcomes, preparing pupils for their next steps into further education, employment, or meaningful participation in the community.
Our staff team regularly reviews progress, adjusting approaches as needed to ensure every pupil continues to feel challenged, supported, and empowered.

‘Nurturing Potential. Inspiring Futures’
Call us: 01730 638010
Welcome to Conifers House School
A New Independent Special School Now Open in Midhurst, West Sussex
Welcome to Conifers House School
A New Independent Special School Now Open in Midhurst, West Sussex
Introducing Our School
Conifers House School is a co-educational, independent Special Educational Needs (SEN) day school for children and young people aged 5 to 16.
‘At Conifers House School, we provide a therapeutic, and inclusive environment to nurture, support, educate and inspire our pupils. We believe neurodivergence is not a barrier but a difference to be celebrated.’
Great Facilities
Our school is purpose-built and expertly designed, complemented with fantastic playing fields and outdoor play and learning facilities.
One-to-One Support
Our children are supported through small class sizes, one-to-one support from expert staff, and a unique, personalised, adapted curriculum.
Nurturing
Our children and young people’s needs, interests and personal development are placed at the heart of their education, complemented by a strong focus on communication and emotional regulation.
Thinking about Conifers House School for your child? Click here to find out more about admissions.
Our Curriculum
Personalised learning for children and young people through our innovative, adapted curriculum pathways:
• Opportunities for Forest School, Swimming, Horse Riding, Outdoor Education and Learning
• Early engagement, with supported sensory learning
• Experiential, topic-based learning
• Life skills and independent learning
• Qualifications and preparation for adulthood
• Embedded therapeutic support through professional therapy provision

pageCache.pageTitle: Enrichment and Outdoor Learning – Conifers House School
pageCache.text:
‘Nurturing Potential. Inspiring Futures’
Call us: 01730 638010
Enrichment and Outdoor Learning
Our enrichment programme is carefully designed to support the personal development, confidence, and wellbeing of every pupil — helping them to explore the world, build new skills, and experience joy in learning.
Outdoor Education
Outdoor learning is an integral part of our curriculum across all pathways. Pupils benefit from regular access to:
Forest School sessions
Sensory play and regulation in natural settings
Exploration of the seasons, environments, and nature
Group challenges and outdoor problem-solving
Physical activity, movement, and space to regulate
Resilience and independence
Social interaction and teamwork
Sensory integration and emotional regulation
Risk-taking in a safe and structured environment
Enrichment Opportunities
We provide a wide range of enriching activities and experiences to help pupils build communication, creativity, curiosity, and confidence. These include:
Swimming and horse riding
Cooking and life skills
Creative therapies (play-based, expressive, and movement-focused)
Cultural days and celebration events
Educational visits and off-site learning experiences
All enrichment activities are carefully planned and adapted to ensure they are accessible, purposeful, and trauma-informed. They form an important part of our commitment to personal development and Preparation for Adulthood.
Learning That Builds Memories
Real-life experiences create lasting memories.
Whether it’s building a den in Forest School, swimming for the first time, or visiting a museum, our enrichment offer is designed to ignite curiosity and make learning meaningful.
We review enrichment offers regularly to ensure they reflect pupil interests, EHCP outcomes, and the evolving needs of our cohort.

‘Nurturing Potential. Inspiring Futures’
Call us: 01730 638010
Curriculum Pathways
Our three pathways provide the flexibility to meet pupils at their current stage of learning while supporting them to progress at their own pace.
Pathways are not fixed by age or key stage. Pupils may remain within a pathway or move between pathways over time, depending on their development and learning profile.
Green Pathway
Learning to Learn
For pupils at the earliest stages of engagement with learning
This pathway supports pupils who may be non-verbal or semi-verbal, require sensory integration, and are working primarily on early developmental, communication, and regulation goals.
Focus areas:
Communication and interaction (AAC, visual supports, intensive interaction)
Emotional regulation and sensory integration
Engagement, attention, and early problem-solving
Developing curiosity and confidence in a learning environment
Approach:
Highly structured, low-arousal environments
Individualised timetables
Specialist interventions and therapeutic input
Learning through play, exploration, and routines
Orange Pathway
Participation in Learning
For pupils beginning to access subject-based learning within a highly supported, practical framework
This pathway supports pupils who are engaging more consistently with structured learning activities and are developing functional communication, independence, and social understanding.
Focus areas:
Functional literacy and numeracy
Communication, emotional regulation, and social skills
Life skills and independence
Topic-based cross-curricular learning
Approach:
Scaffolded subject-specific learning
Visual and practical learning methods
Opportunities for group work, sensory regulation, and real-world application
Regular therapeutic support
Purple Pathway
Independent Learning
For pupils able to access more formal subject learning, with increasing independence and future planning
This pathway supports pupils working towards Entry Level, Functional Skills, and, where appropriate, GCSEs or equivalent qualifications. Preparation for adulthood is embedded throughout.
Focus areas:
Accreditation in English, Maths, ICT, and vocational subjects
Communication and self-advocacy
Independent living and problem-solving
Transition planning, employability, and community access
Approach:
Personalised timetables with subject teachers and support staff
A mix of classroom-based learning and real-life experiences
Emphasis on independence, initiative, and reflection
Continued access to therapy where needed
A Flexible, Needs-Led Model
While each pathway offers a distinct framework, we teach the pupil, not the label. Our staff team regularly reviews progress, adjusting approaches as needed to ensure every pupil continues to feel challenged, supported, and empowered.
Curriculum content across all pathways is linked to National Curriculum objectives, EHCP outcomes, and Preparation for Adulthood goals.
To learn more about how therapy and learning are integrated throughout the school day, visit our Therapies and Wellbeing page.

‘Nurturing Potential. Inspiring Futures’
Call us: 01730 638010
Our Curriculum
Our curriculum is designed to meet the needs of children and young people with autism, communication needs, and complex learning profiles, supported through an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP).
We offer a broad, balanced, and ambitious curriculum that develops communication, independence, emotional regulation, and life skills — all underpinned by therapeutic support and EHCP outcomes.
A Personalised Approach
Every pupil at Conifers follows one of three curriculum pathways: Learning to Learn (Green), Participation in Learning (Orange), or Independent Learning (Purple). These are not fixed by age but are responsive to progress, development, and need.
The pupil’s cognitive profile and learning style
EHCP targets and preparation for adulthood
Social, emotional, and communication needs
Strengths, interests, and motivations
National Curriculum content, adapted and scaffolded
Daily therapeutic strategies
Opportunities to apply learning in real-life contexts
Enrichment experiences beyond the classroom
Foundations for the Future
Whether a pupil is developing early engagement or working towards formal qualifications, our goal is to equip them with the tools to lead a confident, fulfilling life.
Teaching at Conifers is:
Functional literacy and numeracy
Communication skills (including AAC and social communication)
Emotional regulation and wellbeing
Life skills and independence
Creativity, curiosity, and confidence
Multisensory and structured, but responsive and playful
Supported by specialist teaching staff and therapists
Enrichment and Experience
Our curriculum is brought to life through:
These experiences are not extras — they are central to helping our pupils explore the world, practise skills, and develop their voice and identity.
Forest School
Swimming, horse riding, and outdoor education
Creative Arts and play-based learning
Educational visits and community experiences
Regular theme days and cross-curricular projects
Ongoing Review and Development
Our curriculum is reviewed regularly to ensure it:
We use a range of tools — including EHCP reviews, teacher assessment, and therapy input — to monitor progress and adapt plans accordingly.

pageCache.pageTitle: Accreditation and Qualifications – Conifers House School
pageCache.text:
‘Nurturing Potential. Inspiring Futures’
Call us: 01730 638010
Accreditation and Qualifications
We offer a range of certification and accreditation opportunities across all three curriculum pathways. These are designed to be flexible, accessible, and appropriately challenging, and to reflect the diverse needs and strengths of our pupils.
Celebrating Progress Across All Pathways
Pupils may work towards formal or non-formal recognition through:
Pathway Examples
Green Pathway
May include AQA Unit Awards focused on early communication, regulation, interaction, and engagement. Progress is celebrated through sensory and therapeutic milestones.
Orange Pathway
May work towards Entry Level 1 and ASDAN modules in life skills, PSHE, and functional literacy and numeracy. AQA Unit Awards are used to recognise topic work, independence, and communication goals.
Purple Pathway
May access Entry Level Certificates, Functional Skills qualifications, and, where appropriate, GCSEs (Foundation Tier) in subjects such as English, Maths, and Science. Qualification access is carefully matched to cognitive profile, emotional readiness, and EHCP outcomes.
Personalised, Supported Accreditation
We ensure that all accreditation:
Where pupils are not yet ready for formal assessment, progress is tracked through individual targets, portfolios, and evidence-based observations.
Is delivered in a supportive, trauma-informed environment
A Focus on the Future
Every pupil at Conifers House School is supported to leave with:
A portfolio of meaningful achievements
A clear plan for next steps
listItems: Is delivered in a supportive, trauma-informed environment
A clear plan for next steps

‘Nurturing Potential. Inspiring Futures’
Call us: 01730 638010
Careers Programme

We provide downloadable resources, interactive tools and films for educators, front-line workers, families and charities to use with their learners. Young people aged 14+, families and adults can learn directly through the website too.
Employability Skills Progression Map
Best viewed on a larger screen
Financial Education Progression Map
Best viewed on a larger screen
Careers Leader
Our Careers Leader is our Head of School, Catherine Miller.

‘Nurturing Potential. Inspiring Futures’
Call us: 01730 638010
About Us
All of our pupils attend full-time and have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP). We are a small, specialist setting that has been designed to meet the needs of children and young people aged 5 to 16 with autism, communication and interaction needs, and complex learning profiles.
We are proud to be a learning community built on relationships, trust, and inclusion, where every child is seen, heard, and supported to thrive.
What Makes Us Different
At Conifers House School, we provide:
Personalised, pathway-led education for every pupil.
Small class sizes with high staff ratios and strong relational support.
A nurturing, family-style environment with therapeutic principles at its core.
A broad and balanced curriculum, focused on communication, independence, and preparation for adulthood.
An integrated education and therapy model, with daily access to therapeutic input.
Calm, modern learning spaces and generous outdoor facilities.
Staff who are reflective, compassionate, and committed to each pupil’s progress and wellbeing.
Get in touch to find out more – 07815 900586.
Our Vision
To become a leading provider of specialist education in West Sussex and surrounding areas—offering a centre of excellence where pupils with autism and complex needs can flourish, succeed, and live happy, confident lives.
We believe that pupils with SEND deserve exceptional teaching and tailored support. We continually review our practice to ensure it is evidence-based, ambitious, and person-centred, whether supporting early engagement or accredited pathways.
Our team of teachers, therapists, and learning support assistants work in partnership to assess and deliver the right support at the right time—ensuring that pupils build resilience, independence, and a lifelong love for learning.
Our Values
We are a values-driven school. The following core principles underpin every decision we make:
Our Mission
To provide therapeutic, inclusive, and inspiring learning opportunities that support pupils to grow in confidence, develop meaningful skills, and prepare for a successful future.
Our Promise
Our Commitment to Equality
We are committed to upholding the Equality Act 2010 and ensuring protection from discrimination, harassment, or victimisation on the basis of sex, race, disability, religion or belief, gender reassignment, sexual orientation, or pregnancy and maternity. You can view our Equality Statement and Objectives in the Policies section.

‘Nurturing Potential. Inspiring Futures’
Call us: 01730 638010
Admissions
We welcome referrals from local authorities, families, and professionals seeking a therapeutic and personalised education for children with autism, communication needs, and complex learning profiles.
Who We Support
All pupils at Conifers House School will have:
We offer a small, nurturing environment with three curriculum pathways designed to support pupils across a wide range of cognitive profiles and needs. Our approach is best suited to pupils who require a high level of structure, predictability, individual attention, and therapeutic support to thrive in education.
An EHCP in place
Admissions Process
Availability of space within the relevant pathway
Enquiries
Call us: 01730 638010
We look forward to working in partnership with families and local authorities to ensure the best possible outcomes for every pupil.

pageCache.pageTitle: Safeguarding and Well Being – Conifers House School
pageCache.text:
‘Nurturing Potential. Inspiring Futures’
Call us: 01730 638010
Safeguarding and Wellbeing at Conifers House School
At Conifers House School, safeguarding and the well-being of our pupils sit at the very heart of everything we do. We are fully committed to providing the highest standards of care, safety, and protection for every child and young person entrusted to us.
We understand that our pupils’ experiences, vulnerabilities, and needs require an environment where they feel safe, listened to, and respected at all times. Our approach is trauma-informed, nurturing, and proactive, ensuring pupils can build trusting relationships, develop emotional regulation, and feel secure both in school and the wider community.
We support all pupils by:
Safeguarding is everyone’s responsibility
We expect all staff, visitors, and contractors at Conifers House School to behave in ways that ensure our pupils are safeguarded at all times. Any safeguarding concern, no matter how small, must be reported immediately to our Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) or our Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead (DDSL).
Safeguarding Team
Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL): Catherine Miller (Headteacher)
Deputy Designated Safeguarding Leads (DDSL): Georgios Chatzakis (Executive Headteacher)
If you have a safeguarding concern, including during school holidays, please contact our Safeguarding Team.

pageCache.pageTitle: Therapies and Well-being – Conifers House School
pageCache.text:
‘Nurturing Potential. Inspiring Futures’
Call us: 01730 638010
Therapies and Well-being
At Conifers House School, therapy is not a bolt-on — it is woven into the fabric of daily life. We offer an integrated, child-centred approach that places emotional well-being, communication, and sensory regulation at the heart of learning.
Our pupils have complex profiles that often include challenges with emotional regulation, social interaction, and sensory processing. Many have experienced anxiety, trauma, or difficulties accessing previous educational settings.
We aim to create a setting where pupils feel safe, understood, and supported to grow both academically and personally.
Our Therapeutic Offer
Therapies are integrated into both the curriculum and wider school life, ensuring consistent and meaningful support throughout the day.
We offer:
Focused on expressive/receptive language, social communication, and functional communication skills.
Supporting sensory regulation, fine/gross motor development, and access to learning and self-care routines.
Helping pupils process emotions, reduce anxiety, develop self-awareness, and build positive relationships.
Used school-wide to help pupils recognise and manage their emotional states through visual tools, language, and strategies.
Each classroom environment is structured to reduce sensory overload and maximise regulation, predictability, and comfort.
All staff are trained in trauma-informed practice, autism awareness, and therapeutic approaches to behaviour and communication.
Daily Therapeutic Practices Include:
Our goal is to build emotional literacy, resilience, and independence in every pupil — enabling them to engage with learning, form relationships, and prepare for their next steps in life with confidence.
Movement breaks and sensory circuits
Breathing techniques and mindfulness
Access to sensory rooms and quiet spaces
listItems: Access to sensory rooms and quiet spaces

pageCache.text:
‘Nurturing Potential. Inspiring Futures’
Call us: 01730 638010
Welcome to Conifers House School
We offer a nurturing, therapeutic, and inclusive environment where pupils with autism, communication and interaction needs, and complex learning profiles are supported to thrive. All pupils have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) in place.
We believe that neurodivergence is not a barrier to success, but a difference to be understood, supported, and celebrated. At Conifers House School, we have drawn upon the very best practices in SEND education and embedded them into a personalised, pupil-centred approach that is flexible, aspirational, and deeply rooted in each pupil’s unique needs and interests.
Our school is purpose-built with outstanding facilities, complemented by generous outdoor spaces, sensory rooms, and specialist areas supporting learning and wellbeing.

Our Values
At Conifers House School, we are proud to bring an ambitious new provision to West Sussex, shaped by best practice, compassion, and a clear vision for our pupils’ success.
Our curriculum is broad, balanced, and adapted to meet EHCP outcomes, preparing pupils for their next steps into further education, employment, or meaningful participation in the community.
We work closely with families, carers, and professionals, ensuring that our pupils’ voices are heard and that every aspect of our work reflects our values:
These values are woven into our daily life and underpin the vibrant, caring, and ambitious culture we are building at Conifers House School.

Our Vision is Bold:
To become a recognised centre of excellence in West Sussex and beyond, where pupil wellbeing, personal development, and progress go hand in hand, and where every child feels seen, heard, valued, and successful.
We welcome parental and carer engagement at every step of the journey and are proud to say that our success will always be measured by your child’s success, happiness, and confidence.

Welcome to Ash Class
Ash Class is supported by our Teacher, Holly, alongside Teaching Assistants Demiee, Nicky, Kerry and Hayley. We aim to provide a calm, supportive environment where pupils feel safe, valued and ready to learn.
Learning in Ash Class combines structured teaching with practical, multi-sensory experiences to support students’ individual needs and promote independence. Across all lessons, visual aids and strategies tailored to individual students are used, with the overall goal of instilling a love of learning and helping them develop personal confidence.
Our timetable includes daily English and maths, alongside opportunities to develop communication, social skills and independence throughout the day. Pupils have access to a broad and balanced curriculum, including regular outdoor learning through Forest School, to support confidence, teamwork and wellbeing.
